26 A double-slit interference pattern using red light of wavelength 7.0 × 10–7
m has a fringe spacing
of 3.5 mm.
m?
Which fringe spacing would be observed for the same arrangement of apparatus but using blue
light of wavelength 4.5 × 10–7
A
2.3 mm
B
3.5 mm
C
5.4 mm
D
9.0 mm

hints: Notice the same apparatus is used, so slit separation $a$ and screen distance $D$ are unchanged and only wavelength $\lambda$ changes from $7.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ to $4.5 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
Recall fringe spacing $x = \lambda D / a$, so for fixed $D$ and $a$ the new $3.5 \text{ mm}$ spacing scales by the wavelength ratio.
Calculate $3.5 \text{ mm}$ multiplied by $4.5/7.0$ and check whether the result should be smaller than $3.5 \text{ mm}$ because blue light has shorter wavelength.
walkthrough: Identify the given data: $\lambda_{red} = 7.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ gives $x_{red} = 3.5 \text{ mm}$, and $\lambda_{blue} = 4.5 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ with the same $a$ and $D$.
State the governing rule: double-slit fringe spacing is $x = \lambda D / a$, so $x$ is directly proportional to $\lambda$ when $D$ and $a$ are constant.
Set up the ratio: $x_{blue} / x_{red} = \lambda_{blue} / \lambda_{red}$, so $x_{blue} = 3.5 \text{ mm} \times (4.5 \times 10^{-7})/(7.0 \times 10^{-7})$.
Calculate the intermediate result: $4.5/7.0 \approx 0.643$, then $3.5 \text{ mm} \times 0.643 \approx 2.25 \text{ mm}$, which rounds to $2.3 \text{ mm}$ with correct length unit.
Connect to the options: a shorter wavelength must give a smaller spacing than $3.5 \text{ mm}$, and $2.3 \text{ mm}$ matches this calculation. This is option A.

A.explanation: Fringe spacing scales with wavelength, so $3.5 \text{ mm} \times 4.5/7.0 \approx 2.3 \text{ mm}$.

B.explanation: Spacing cannot stay at $3.5 \text{ mm}$ because fringe spacing $x$ is directly proportional to wavelength $\lambda$.

C.explanation: This uses the inverse ratio $7.0/4.5$, which would increase $x$ for shorter blue wavelength instead of decreasing it.

D.explanation: This value is much larger than $3.5 \text{ mm}$, whereas changing from $7.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ to $4.5 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ must reduce the spacing.
